questions.question: Which of the following computer type has a better monitor and a more powerful microprocessor?
Which of the following was the first general-purpose electronic digital computer designed for corporate applications in the United States?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**UNIVAC I**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **UNIVAC I (Universal Automatic Computer I)** was the first general-purpose electronic digital computer designed for corporate and business applications in the USA.
 
• It was developed by **J. Presper Eckert** and **John Mauchly**, the same engineers who created ENIAC.
 
• UNIVAC I was first delivered in **1951** to the U.S. Census Bureau.
 
• Unlike ENIAC, which was mainly used for military and scientific purposes, UNIVAC I was designed for **commercial data processing**.
 
• It used **vacuum tube technology** and magnetic tape for data storage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/30ac29028c0754814b1749368b30a020a515d58ac81d4a629a2557188564e043.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Comparison with Other Options:**

 
 
• **Z3 Machine:** Built by Konrad Zuse in Germany (1941); not used for corporate applications.
 
• **ENIAC:** First electronic digital computer, but mainly for military calculations.
 
• **Turing Machine:** A theoretical model, not a real physical computer.
 
• **UNIVAC I:** First commercial, general-purpose electronic digital computer for business use.
 
 
 
• **Historical Significance:**
 
 
• UNIVAC I correctly predicted the **1952 U.S. presidential election**.
 
• It marked the beginning of the **commercial computing era**.
 
 
 
• **Important Facts:**
 
 
• Used mercury delay lines for memory.
 
• Weighed around 13 tons.
 
• Cost about $1 million per unit.

questions.question: First computer was installed in India at :
questions.solution:
**The correct option is (4) "Indian Statistical Institute, Kolkata"**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The first digital computer in India was a British-made HEC 2M machine that was placed in the Indian Statistical Institute in Kolkata in 1955.
 
• The device was formally inaugurated in February 1960 and eventually given the name TIFRAC (TIFR Automatic Calculator) in 1962 when the new TIFR buildings were opened by Jawaharlal Nehru, the country's then-prime minister.
 
• The HEC-2M created by A.D. Booth and placed at the Indian Statistical Institute (ISI) in Calcutta in 1955 marked the beginning of computing in India.
 
• The Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR) in Mumbai began developing a digital computer in 1955 under the direction of Rangaswami Narasimhan.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In December 2002, the PARAM Padma was presented. In June 2003, this was the first Indian supercomputer to appear on a ranking of the fastest supercomputers in the world.
 
• Any of a class of machines known as digital computers are able to solve issues by processing data in discrete form.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are true?

(i) VDU stands for visual display unit and is an example of both software and hardware.

(ii) Interpreter is used for assembly language programs, while compiler is used for high level language programs.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Neither (i) nor (ii)**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• (i) **VDU stands for Visual Display Unit,** but it is an example of **hardware**, not **software**. It refers to a **computer monitor or display screen**.
 
• (ii) **Interpreters **and **compilers **are both used for** high-level language programs**.
 
 
• An **interpreter** **translates and executes code line by line, while a compiler translates the entire source code of a program into machine code before executing it.**
 
• Assembly language programs typically use assemblers, not interpreters or compilers, to convert assembly language into machine code.

questions.question: The first generation computers can be characterized as _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Digital computer**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **computing technology generation**, the **first era** was from **1946 to 1959**.
 
• The** first generation **of computers used **vacuum tubes** for the basic components of **memory** and the circuitry of the CPU (Central Processing Unit).
 
• These tubes, like light bulbs, produced a** lot of heat** and **frequently melted **equipment. They were therefore very **expensive** and only **large organisations **could afford them.
 
• The** first-generation computers** can be characterised as **Digital computer**.
 
• This generation used primarily **batch processing operating systems**.
 
• **Punched cards, punched tapes** and **magnetic tapes** were used as **input **and **output devices**.
 
• Computers of this generation used **machine language** as their **programming language**.
 
• **ENIAC, EDVAC, UNIVAC, IBM-701 **and **IBM-650** are the computers used in this first generation of computing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Second-generation computer: **In the second-generation computer, the technology used is a** transistor**. The material used behind the transistor is made of a **semiconductor**.
 
• **Third-generation computer:** In the third-generation computer, the technology used is an **IC or Integrated Circuit**. In this generation,** high-level language** is used.
 
• **Fourth-generation computer:** In the fourth-generation computer, the technology used is **VLSI **and **microprocessor**.
 
• **Fifth-generation computer: **In the fifth-generation computer, the technology used is **ULSI technology**.

questions.question: Which of the following facts is incorrect regarding the control unit of the computer?

options.text: It receives instructions from memory, interprets them, and directs the operation of the computer.
It manages and coordinates all the units of the computer.
It is responsible for controlling the transfer of data and instructions between other units of the computer.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It processes and stores data**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

The control unit (CU) is a crucial component of the computer's central processing unit (CPU). Here's a brief explanation of why each statement is correct or incorrect:

__
 
• **It receives instructions from memory, interprets them, and directs the operation of the computer.**

 
 
• **Correct**. The control unit fetches instructions from the computer's memory, decodes them to understand what specific operations need to be performed, and then directs the other parts of the CPU to execute those operations.
 
 
 
• **It processes and stores data.**
 
 
• **Incorrect**. The processing and storage of data are primarily the functions of the arithmetic logic unit (ALU) and memory/storage components, not the control unit. The ALU performs arithmetic and logical operations, while different types of memory (like RAM, hard drives, etc.) are responsible for storing data.
 
 
 
• **It manages and coordinates all the units of the computer.**
 
 
• **Correct**. The control unit coordinates the activities of all other units within the computer, ensuring that they work in harmony and follow the instructions of the currently executing program.
 
 
 
• **It is responsible for controlling the transfer of data and instructions between other units of the computer.**
 
 
• **Correct**. The control unit manages the flow of data and instructions between the CPU, memory, and peripheral devices, making sure that the right data is in the right place at the right time for processing.
 
 

Therefore, the statement "It processes and stores data" is incorrect regarding the functions of the control unit.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The word **computer **is derived from the word **compute**. In the **year 1833**, English **mechanical engineer Charles Babbage** designed the first **analytical engine**. He is known as the **father of the computer**.
 
• In the beginning, computers are used for calculating large numbers and can only store a small amount of data.

questions.question:
Booting instructions are stored inside :

1) Floppy disk

2) ROM

3) RAM

4) Operating system
questions.solution:
• Booting instructions, also known as firmware or BIOS, are stored in a non-volatile memory device called ROM (Read-Only Memory).
 
• This means that the instructions are permanently stored in the ROM and cannot be altered or deleted.
 
• When a computer is powered on, the BIOS instructions are loaded into the RAM, where they are executed to start the boot process and load the operating system.
 
• Floppy disks and Operating system are not used to store Booting instructions.

questions.question: Which of the following codes provides a way through which an individual character can be represented in the form of web pages, text files and other documents, which can be used to represent characters from all languages around the world?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Unicode**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Unicode: **As explained earlier, it's a character encoding standard that is used to represent characters from practically **all languages, and miscellaneous symbols**. It includes over a **million characters**. Each character in Unicode has a **unique number** - its code point, making it universally standardized.
 
• **Extended ASCII:** ASCII stands for **American Standard Code for Information Interchange**. The original **ASCII is a 7-bit character set** and** includes 128 characters**, including **English letters, numbers, various punctuation, and control characters**. Extended ASCII is an 8-bit character set and includes an additional 128 characters to meet the demands of representing more characters and non-English languages, although it is still not enough to cover all languages especially non-Latin based ones.
 
• **ASCII:** As I mentioned before, A**SCII is a 7-bit character set that includes 128 characters**. It was originally designed for English and includes English letters, numbers, punctuation, and control characters. It doesn't have the capability to represent a wide range of international characters.
 
• **Binary: **Binary is** not a character encoding**, but a **base-2 number system** that computers use to represent and process all data, not just text. Typically, binary is used to refer to **sequences of bits** that represent **numeric **or **logical values** in computing. In terms of text, binary doesn't directly encode letters or symbols. However, all character encoding schemes, including ASCII and Unicode, ultimately use binary to represent characters because computers understand binary.
